summary.intent: Address two review findings (Medium: memory retention; Low: error ordering) on change 46 (PR #74, parallel text search) in the monokl crate.
summary.outcome: Started a focused agent fix on the `perf/match-path` branch with files modified in text_search.rs and a new memory test. Nothing is verified, pushed, or resolved yet; the findings remain open.

repo: Change 46 corresponds to trail 285 and PR #74 (parallel search), on branch `perf/match-path`.
Parallel search in #74 collects all per-file hit buffers before applying `max_files`, so discarded files stay resident together; previously buffers were dropped one file at a time.
The library contract in text_search.rs lines 65-68 says results are reported 'in walk order', and the deferred error/outcome merging breaks this.
Rust-support work (in `analysis/`) runs in parallel and touches different files than the text_search.rs fix, so conflicts are not expected.
CI is `just ci`, and a harness checks output byte-identity on at least 40 queries across the pinned repos.

code.finding: Collecting all outcomes at line 185 retains every file's complete hit buffer before `max_files` is applied at lines 195-198. Fix is to process bounded, ordered batches, drop hits past the ceiling immediately, and keep counting excess matches so `files_total` stays exact.

The walk records an unlistable `z/` error at line 155 before the deferred loop at line 186 records an unreadable `a.ts`, reversing the previous order. Fix is to keep traversal positions for walk errors and file outcomes and merge them in that order.

workflow: Each review finding must first be reproduced by a failing test before being fixed.
Acceptance is judged by exit codes (`just ci` and the harness), not by the agent's own claims.
Guard performance: the batching must not give up more than 5% of #74's zod speedup.
Push to the same branch without force, and resolve only the findings that were reproduced and fixed, recording the fix on each finding.
Memory-bound tests should make the bound observable rather than rely on timing.

friction: The medium finding was a known caveat from the parallel search design that was flagged when #74 landed, so it shipped with a known memory regression.
The ordering regression came from deferring file outcomes after walk errors, a subtle behavior change from parallelizing.
open_items: Confirm the agent's fix passes `just ci` and the byte-identical harness, then pushes to `perf/match-path` and resolves the findings.
After the held-out question set lands, measure #74 and #75 (Rust support) combined against rg.
Verify the batching stays within the 5% zod speedup budget.
